The screen

Every image below is a PNG rendered straight from the app's own canvas — the same code path that draws the window on a Mac. Nothing here is a mockup of a screen that does not exist.

The whole window is painted on one canvas. There is not a single native button, tab or checkbox in the main view, and that is deliberate: the operating system's own widgets look different on macOS, Windows and Linux and cannot do gradients or rounded corners, so the layout would have drifted apart on each machine. Painting it means one appearance everywhere — and it means the screen can be rendered to a PNG with no display attached, which is how the layout is checked.

The left rail

Five icons, each a page rather than a dialog. The Market Map used to open in its own window; it is a page now, which gives it the whole area instead of a third of it.

IconPage
Pulsethe signal board — the Signal and Chart tabs
GridMarket Map, the sector heat map, full width
BarsYour trades — the summary of everything closed
Bella switch, not a destination: popup alerts on or off
GearSettings — token state, where credentials live, which files get written

The icons are spaced by solving for the room between the logo and the theme toggle rather than by a fixed pitch, so the rail stays clear of the bottom controls at every window size the app allows.

Reading the signal board

PartWhat it is telling you
Signal ticketthe call itself — BUY CE, BUY PE, or nothing. OPEN means it is live and tracked; PREVIEW means a direction exists but no ticket was issued; DEMO means the figures are not live data.
Entry / Nowthe premium at issue, and the premium now. The rupee figure beside them is that difference across your chosen lots.
Reward : riskthe ratio computed at entry from ATR. Below the floor it never became a ticket at all.
T1 / T2 / T3the three targets, each with how far price has travelled toward it — a check mark and a timestamp once reached.
Stopwith the same progress bar, which is the one you actually want to be watching.
Confidencethe dial, with every input that fed it listed underneath. A dash means that input abstained and was ignored rather than counted as neutral.
Market trendthe plain-English label — RANGE-BOUND / CHOPPY, MODERATE DOWNTREND — with the ADX reading and how far price has actually displaced in ATR terms.
Sessioneverything closed today, in order, with the running total split into booked and open.

Not investment advice. NBS Signal Tool is a decision-support screen that applies a fixed, published rule set to index data. It is not the output of a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser, no recommendation is being made to any person, and no order is ever placed by this software. Trading index options can lose you your entire capital. The rule set was measured across three years of history and returned a negative expectancy after costs — the figures are here. You are responsible for anything you do with what you see.
NBS Signal Tool

A rule-based second opinion on Nifty, Bank Nifty and Sensex index options. It shows its working, it says WAIT most of the time, and it places no orders.
